pillars.name: Giving isn't down, it moved
pillars.definition: The sector-level read on donor behavior: dollars up, donor base narrowing, and generosity reorganizing along identifiable fault lines — ROI, privacy, anonymity, frustration, access — rather than disappearing.
in_scope: DAFs and giving that never appears in a file
what a shrinking base means for strategy
pillars.why_now: As CEO he is the right seat for the sector-level thesis, and the data refreshed this quarter: FEP Q1 2026 shows dollars +4.3% with donor counts -0.8%, retention at 18% (vs 18.2% in 2024), repeat donors now ~61% of dollars and recaptured donors another 15%; CCS's 2026 Philanthropy Pulse has 68% of nonprofits naming acquisition as a top challenge. His queued post cites the older annual cut.

pillars.name: They left because they stopped feeling seen
pillars.definition: Why donors lapse and what brings them back: the receipt that says nothing, the only-mail-is-an-ask pattern, and the case that recapture is a bigger revenue line than most organizations staff for.
in_scope: what each touchpoint builds or burns
pillars.why_now: There is a live tension worth publishing: his queued post says only ~2% of lapsed donors ever return, while the Q1 2026 FEP cut shows recaptured donors contributing ~15% of all dollars. Both can be true, and the gap between them is the argument — recapture is undervalued precisely because the per-donor odds look bad.

proof_assets.notes: Pair with the Q1 2026 recapture figure for the tension
